newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Tulip sees sales growth in Asia - paper.
newsitem.headline: Tulip sees sales growth in Asia - paper.

text.p: Dutch personal computer maker Tulip Computers NV plans to achieve rapid sales growth in Asia in the next few years, according to a report on Wednesday in Dutch evening newspaper NRC Handelsblad.

"I expect that, in five years' time, half of our turnover will come from Asia," Tulip chairman Rob Romein was quoted as saying. The NRC Handelsblad article said Tulip now generates about five percent of its turnover in Asia.
Tulip has set up an Asian reqional headquarters and an assembly plant in Hong Kong in 1995. Romein was quoted as saying Tulip wanted to break even in Asia after three years.
"We got off to a slower start than we expected. The start- up costs turned out higher, but in the meantime things are going reasonably well," he said.
He said Asian personal computer markets were growing at 25 to 30 percent per year, compared with 12 percent in Europe.
Tulip announced on Tuesday that it broke off exploratory partnership talks with an unnamed company, but Romein said Tulip would continue to look for partners.
"We will continue to look actively at cooperation with other companies, but at the moment we have not taken any firm decision about new steps," he said.
